title: Iran Submits 14-Point Peace Proposal — Demands Hormuz Unblocking, Full Sanctions Relief, and Withdrawal Within 30 Days
detail: Iran submitted a formal 14-point response to the US proposal to end the conflict on May 2, 2026 — Day 64 — transmitted through Pakistani mediators in Islamabad. Iran's proposal was notably more expansive than the Hormuz-first framework it had floated on May 1: it demanded the US lift its naval blockade, withdraw all US forces from the region, release all frozen Iranian assets, pay war reparations, lift all sanctions, and end military operations on all fronts including Lebanon — all within 30 days rather than the US-proposed two-month ceasefire window. Iran's Foreign Ministry confirmed the submission. The proposal was described by Al Jazeera as Iran's most comprehensive peace terms to date, consolidating earlier five-point and Hormuz-first frameworks into a single document. Pakistan's mediators called the Iranian submission a serious basis for negotiation. Iran framed the 30-day timeline as a confidence-building measure, arguing a shorter window reduced the risk of either side using talks as cover to rebuild military capacity. US officials privately characterized the proposal as requiring significant renegotiation on nuclear terms before any formal response would be issued. The ceasefire that began April 8 remained nominally in effect on Day 64, but the IRGC warned separately on the same day that resumed conflict was 'possible' if no deal was reached.

media.caption: Iran submits 14-point peace proposal via Pakistani mediators on Day 64 — demands US withdrawal, sanctions relief, and Hormuz unblocking within 30 days

title: Trump Declares 'Not Satisfied' with Iran's 14-Point Offer — IRGC Warns Renewed Conflict 'Possible'
detail: President Trump responded to Iran's 14-point peace proposal on May 2, 2026 — Day 64 — by publicly stating he was 'not satisfied' with Tehran's offer. Speaking to reporters, Trump said: 'They want to make a deal, I'm not satisfied with it, so we'll see what happens.' The statement dashed early optimism that followed Iran's submission through Pakistani mediators and deepened uncertainty about when or whether a formal framework for peace could be agreed. The central sticking point remained Iran's omission of binding nuclear commitments acceptable to Washington. Simultaneously, a senior IRGC military official issued a stark warning that renewed armed conflict was 'possible' if negotiations continued to stall, and that 'surprise measures are planned for the enemy, beyond their imagination.' The dual development — an Iranian diplomatic offer and a concurrent IRGC military threat — underscored the fractured nature of Iranian decision-making between the Pezeshkian government and the IRGC. Analysts noted the IRGC's warning, delivered through state media, was timed to maximize psychological pressure on both the US and Iran's own civilian diplomats. The Al Jazeera live blog reported the situation as entering a particularly dangerous phase: Iran was submitting proposals while its military simultaneously threatened escalation, leaving Washington uncertain which Iranian actor to negotiate with.

media.caption: Trump declares 'not satisfied' with Iran's 14-point offer on Day 64 as IRGC warns renewed conflict 'possible'
